methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native directly target capability distribution outside elite hubs, exemplifying peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could enable broad fluency if scaled beyond individual initiative.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA represents institutional infrastructure for distributed learning beyond NoVA, signaling potential for regional capability centers that could compete with concentration dynamics if adequately resourced.

signals.title: Virginia Tech, Children’s National Spark Pediatric AI Innovation Hub to Speed Research, Care | Newswise - Newswise
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech-Children's National collaboration creates deep research capability but concentrates specialized AI-healthcare expertise in institutional nodes, reinforcing hub dominance unless deliberately designed for knowledge diffusion to rural health systems.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece explicitly identifies AI data centers as accelerating urban-rural divide, signaling infrastructure investment that brings economic activity to NoVA while imposing costs (power, land use) without distributing capability or workforce development.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: AI use strong in Virginia, with Montgomery County at No. 5 statewide - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Montgomery County ranking fifth statewide in AI usage suggests Virginia Tech is enabling deep distributed capability in traditionally non-metro areas, demonstrating university-anchored diffusion models that could scale across Appalachian and rural regions.
